description: Replace deploy/setup.sh with an idempotent, subcommand-driven script whose primary job is fast iteration on a headless Pi. The existing file is a draft that must not be shipped: it overwrites /opt/pantry/.env on every run (destroying a pinned PANTRY_IMAGE_TAG and then redeploying latest), never copies the systemd/ or udev/ subdirectories it later reads from, and writes a literal unexpanded $(dpkg --print-architecture) into an apt sources file. The highest-value addition is a `status` subcommand that walks the whole chain from udev rule to /health scanner state and prints exactly which link is broken, so an attempt takes seconds to diagnose instead of minutes of guessing.
steps: Read the current deploy/setup.sh in full before changing it. It is easier to rewrite than to patch; a rewrite is expected. Preserve nothing that is not called for below.

Establish a SCRIPT_DIR at the top: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)". Every source-file read must be relative to SCRIPT_DIR. Every destination write goes to /opt/pantry. The current script conflates the two — it copies from the working directory but reads systemd/ and udev/ from /opt/pantry, which is why a fresh install fails.

Implement subcommands dispatched from "$1": `install`, `rule`, `status`, `logs`, `freeze`, `thaw`, and `help`. Default to `help` when no subcommand is given — never default to a mutating action. Use [[ "$VAR" == true ]] for boolean tests; do not execute a variable as a command the way the current script does with `if ! $SCANNER_ONLY`.

`install` must converge idempotently in this order: (1) verify root via EUID, (2) ensure Docker and the compose plugin are present, installing via `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh` if absent — use the convenience script the README already specifies, and DELETE the current hand-rolled apt-repository path entirely along with its broken escaped-$() sources line and its non-idempotent `gpg --dearmor` call, (3) add ${SUDO_USER:-$USER} to the docker group, never bare $USER which is root or empty under sudo, (4) copy the whole deploy tree from SCRIPT_DIR to /opt/pantry including systemd/ and udev/ and setup.sh itself, excluding .env, (5) reconcile .env, (6) ensure /dev/input exists, (7) install the udev rule, (8) bring the container up, (9) poll health, (10) print status.

Reconcile .env instead of overwriting it. If /opt/pantry/.env does not exist, create it from .env.example. If it does exist, append ONLY keys that appear in .env.example and are absent from .env, and never modify a key that already has a value. Print each key added. This is the single most important behavioral fix: the current `cp .env.example .env` silently resets a pinned PANTRY_IMAGE_TAG and the subsequent `up -d` then redeploys latest, defeating the documented rollback procedure.

Ensure the bind-mount source exists before starting the container: if /dev/input is absent, create it. If the directory does not exist, Docker will auto-create the bind-mount source as an ordinary directory on the root filesystem, which will never reflect device nodes udev creates in devtmpfs, and the scanner will silently never be found. Record a warning if it had to be created, since it means no input device has ever been attached.

Implement udev rule generation — do not ask the operator to hand-edit a template. Detect candidate scanners by reading /proc/bus/input/devices and, when usbutils is present, `lsusb`. Match by more than the literal word 'scanner': many scanners present as generic HID keyboards. When more than one candidate exists and the session is interactive, present a numbered picker; when non-interactive, fail with the candidate list rather than guessing. From the chosen device emit /etc/udev/rules.d/99-pantry-scanner.rules containing one active rule in the form: SUBSYSTEM=="input", KERNEL=="event*", ENV{ID_VENDOR_ID}=="<vid>", ENV{ID_MODEL_ID}=="<pid>", SYMLINK+="input/pantry-scanner", GROUP="65532", MODE="0640" — and for a Bluetooth device, match ATTRS{name} instead. Write the file only when its content differs from what is already installed, so re-runs are quiet. Then `udevadm control --reload` and `udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=input --action=add`. Scope the trigger to the input subsystem; a bare `udevadm trigger --action=add` re-fires add for every device on the box.

Do NOT add TAG+="systemd", ENV{SYSTEMD_WANTS}, or ENV{SYSTEMD_ALIAS} to the generated rule, and do not install or reference a pantry.service unit. Under Design B the container is always running, so a scanner appearing needs no container action at all — the app's own reconnect loop picks it up within 30 seconds.

`rule` runs only the detection and rule-generation steps plus the reload and trigger, then prints status. This replaces the current --scanner-only flag, which was not scanner-only: it still clobbered .env and still required docker-compose.yml in the working directory.

Implement `status` as the diagnostic centerpiece. Print one line per link with PASS / FAIL / SKIP and, on FAIL, the exact remediation command. The chain, in order: (1) /opt/pantry deployment files present; (2) .env present, echoing the effective PANTRY_IMAGE_TAG, HOST_PORT and SCANNER_DEVICE; (3) /dev/input exists and is on devtmpfs; (4) /etc/udev/rules.d/99-pantry-scanner.rules exists and contains at least one non-comment rule; (5) SCANNER_DEVICE resolves — `readlink -f` it and report the concrete event node; (6) that node's group is 65532 and mode is 0640; (7) container is running per `docker compose ps`; (8) GET /health on the effective HOST_PORT returns status ok; (9) the health payload's scanner object — connected, grabbed, lastError, unmappedKeys; (10) whether pantry-update.timer is active, masked, or absent.

In `status`, treat an absent scanner as a PASS-with-note, not a failure. Under Design B a missing scanner is a fully supported state: the container must still be running and /health must still return ok. The failure the operator cares about is a scanner that is PRESENT but unreadable — node exists yet health reports connected:false with a permission error, which means the rule's GROUP does not match the container's GID 65532. Make those two cases visibly different in the output.

Read HOST_PORT from the reconciled .env and use it for every health check and every printed URL. The current script hardcodes 8080 in both verify_service and the closing banner, so any operator who set HOST_PORT gets a spurious failure warning and a URL that does not work.

Replace the fixed `sleep 3` health check with polling against a deadline of at least 60 seconds, since a first-run image pull on a Pi routinely exceeds three seconds. On timeout, fail loudly and dump `docker compose logs --tail=50 pantry`. Do not print a success banner after a failed verification the way the current script does.

Implement `freeze` and `thaw` to `systemctl mask --now pantry-update.timer` and `systemctl unmask pantry-update.timer` respectively. Explain in `help` why this matters: the timer fires every five minutes, pulls latest, and recreates the container, so leaving it enabled while iterating mutates the target mid-experiment and makes results irreproducible.
Do not enable pantry-update.timer during `install` by default. Add an explicit `--with-updates` flag for when iteration is finished. The current script enables it unconditionally.

Implement `logs` to show recent container output — `docker compose -f /opt/pantry/docker-compose.yml logs --tail=100 -f pantry`. Note in `help` that the image is distroless so `docker exec` into a shell is not available and container logs plus /health are the only runtime introspection.

Make per-step fatality explicit. A fatal step must log an error with a remediation hint and `exit 1`; an advisory step must warn and continue. Do not rely on a bare `return 1` propagating through `set -e` the way install_udev_rules currently does — under `set -euo pipefail` that aborts the whole run silently, after .env has already been damaged.
Guard color output with a TTY check so redirecting to a log file does not embed escape codes, and stop emitting a colored INFO prefix for intentionally blank lines.

Delete the dead code from the current script rather than carrying it forward: configure_env (greps and logs, writes nothing), configure_scanner (its three guards can never fire because .env.example already contains all three keys), the `command -v docker compose` check (command -v takes one operand, so it tests for docker and reports on compose), and the unused `installed` variable in check_existing_installation.

Verify syntax with `bash -n deploy/setup.sh`. shellcheck is not installed in this sandbox; attempt `apt-get install -y shellcheck` and run it if that succeeds, otherwise record in findings that shellcheck was unavailable and the script was reviewed by reading. Do not claim a clean shellcheck run that did not happen.

Add a shellcheck step to .github/workflows/ci.yml so this class of defect is caught mechanically in future. Several items above — the escaped-$() sources line, bare $USER, the one-operand command -v, the unused variable — are all things shellcheck flags automatically.
Commit with a message like `feat: rewrite deploy setup script with status diagnostics`.
acceptance_criteria: deploy/setup.sh dispatches install, rule, status, logs, freeze, thaw, help, and defaults to help rather than to a mutating action.
Running install twice in a row is safe: an existing .env is never overwritten, and a pinned PANTRY_IMAGE_TAG survives a second run.
The script reads every source file relative to SCRIPT_DIR and copies the full deploy tree, including systemd/ and udev/, to /opt/pantry.
The udev rule is generated from a detected device, contains SYMLINK+="input/pantry-scanner", GROUP="65532", MODE="0640", and contains no TAG+="systemd", ENV{SYSTEMD_WANTS}, or ENV{SYSTEMD_ALIAS}.
The script ensures /dev/input exists before starting the container.
status prints all ten chain links with PASS/FAIL/SKIP, distinguishes 'scanner absent (supported)' from 'scanner present but unreadable', and prints a remediation command for each failure.
HOST_PORT is read from .env and used for every health check and printed URL; 8080 is not hardcoded.
The health check polls against a deadline of at least 60s and no success banner is printed after a failed verification.
install does not enable pantry-update.timer unless --with-updates is passed; freeze and thaw mask and unmask it.
The hand-rolled apt repository path, configure_env, configure_scanner, the `command -v docker compose` check, and the unused `installed` variable are all gone.
`bash -n deploy/setup.sh` exits 0, and .github/workflows/ci.yml contains a shellcheck step.
verification: `bash deploy/setup.sh help` and `bash deploy/setup.sh` (no args) both print usage and exit 0 without requiring root and without mutating anything.
`grep -n 'cp .*\.env\.example.*\.env' deploy/setup.sh` shows the copy is guarded by an existence test, not unconditional.

`grep -n 'SCRIPT_DIR' deploy/setup.sh` shows source reads are relative to it; `grep -n '/opt/pantry/systemd\|/opt/pantry/udev' deploy/setup.sh` shows those paths used only as destinations or in status checks, never as the source of a copy.
`grep -n 'subsystem-match=input' deploy/setup.sh` shows the scoped trigger; a bare `udevadm trigger --action=add` appears nowhere.
`grep -n '8080' deploy/setup.sh` shows 8080 only as a documented default fallback, never as the port used for an actual health request.
`grep -n 'configure_env\|configure_scanner\|command -v docker compose' deploy/setup.sh` produces no output.

KNOWN SANDBOX GAP: udevadm and shellcheck are not installed here, so rule-file syntax and shell linting cannot be verified locally. Record this in findings and defer both to FEAT-005. Do not claim either was verified.
